title: Operational readiness checklist for perf-regression canary (rollback, ownership, SLAs, maintenance windows)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Create and publish an operational readiness checklist for the perf-regression canary rollout. This is the “ready to page humans” bar: defined rollback actions, clear ownership boundaries, response SLAs, and maintenance/suppression guidance so we don’t create pager fatigue or ambiguous escalation paths.

Scope
- Deploy rollback plan: what gets rolled back (runtime build vs canary config vs alert rules), by whom, and how quickly.
- Ownership handoff: SRE vs Runtime responsibilities during triage and confirmation.
- SLAs for alert response: expected initial response, confirmation, and escalation windows.
- Maintenance windows + suppression guidelines: how to suppress during deploys / warmups without hiding real regressions.

References
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Runbook+-+Perf+Canary+Regression+Triage
- Alert policy: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/Perf+Regression+Alert+Policy
- Baseline ADR (deploy windows + suppression rationale): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0231+-+Perf+Regression+Baseline+Strategy
- Dashboard inventory: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PLAT/Perf+Canary+Dashboards

Operational readiness checklist (v1)

A) Preconditions to enable paging (gate)
[ ] Canary traffic classified as canary-safe (rate limited + low priority) in runtime and verified in one region.
[ ] Canary metrics label schema matches cardinality budget (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode only) and has passed the label-schema integration test suite.
[ ] Dashboards exist for: per-model p95 latency, per-model tokens/sec, and slice drilldowns (gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode).
[ ] Alert rules in “ticket-only” mode for >= 72h with backtest results documented and reviewed by SRE.
[ ] Runbook published and linked in alert payload.
[ ] PagerDuty service + routing rule exists and test pages have been acknowledged.

B) Ownership + escalation policy
Primary flow (who does what)
- SRE is first responder for perf-canary regression pages to validate signal quality and determine if this is “production perf risk” vs “canary artifact.”
- Runtime is the escalation owner once confirmed (or earlier if strong runtime-deploy correlation).

RACI (v1)
- Signal validation (sample size, suppression correctness, slice sanity): SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes).
- Root cause investigation (kernel selection, scheduler behavior, runtime regressions): Runtime (Noah Patel / Hiro Tanaka / Sofia Ivanova).
- Metrics pipeline / aggregation bugs: Telemetry (Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman / Caleb Johnson).

Handoff criteria (SRE -> Runtime)
[ ] Regression persists beyond warmup window and is present in at least one stable slice (gpu_sku pinned).
[ ] Not within an approved maintenance window OR regression magnitude exceeds “ignore during deploy” threshold.
[ ] Baseline comparison is consistent across p95 + tokens/sec (or otherwise explained in notes).
[ ] Alert payload includes runtime_build + runtime_version/git_sha; if missing, file immediate bug and route to Telemetry.

C) Alert response SLAs (internal)
- Page acknowledgement: 10 minutes (24/7 oncall).
- Initial validation (noise vs real): 30 minutes.
- If confirmed regression: escalate to Runtime oncall / #eng-runtime within 45 minutes.
- Mitigation decision (rollback vs suppress vs continue monitoring): within 90 minutes of initial page.

Severity mapping guidance
- Sev2 (page): >= 8% p95 regression sustained for 30m OR >= 10% tokens/sec drop sustained for 30m in a critical model/region slice.
- Sev3 (ticket): smaller regressions (e.g., 4–8%) or regressions limited to non-critical slices; no immediate action required.

D) Rollback / mitigation plan
Rollback decision tree
1) If correlated with a runtime deploy (annotation within last 2h): prefer runtime rollback to last known-good runtime build.
2) If correlated with canary runner config change only: rollback canary config to previous revision (model list / prompt set / warmup settings).
3) If correlated with telemetry/aggregation change: disable new aggregation path or revert alert rule to previous version; keep canary running for raw-signal collection.
4) If regression appears isolated to a single gpu_sku: quarantine that sku from canary routing (and separately evaluate fleet impact).

Actions (mechanical)
- Runtime rollback: release train owner (Connor O’Brien) + Runtime oncall execute rollback via standard runtime deploy tooling; confirm via deploy annotations in Grafana.
- Canary runner rollback: revert perf-canary deployment (GitHub perf-canary repo) and/or config in region; ensure canary remains “small and safe.”
- Alert rollback: revert observability-pack alert rule PR / last rule version; confirm dedup keys unchanged.

Post-rollback verification
[ ] p95 and tokens/sec return to baseline band within 60m.
[ ] Confirm no accidental suppression masking the issue.
[ ] Open follow-up issue for root cause + permanent fix (assign to Runtime/Telemetry accordingly).

E) Maintenance windows + suppression guidelines
Definitions
- Maintenance window: approved interval where alerts may be suppressed due to expected instability (deploy, node churn, planned cache flush).
- Suppression is scoped by (region, model, runtime_build) where possible; global suppressions require SRE lead approval.

Rules
- Suppress only during the deploy window + fixed warmup buffer (default: deploy duration + 20 minutes).
- Never suppress when regression magnitude exceeds “critical override” threshold (default: >= 15% p95 regression or >= 20% tokens/sec drop sustained for 15m).
- Always annotate suppression start/end in #eng-oncall and in the incident timeline if paging was active.

Approval + documentation
- Planned maintenance: SRE opens a short ticket or posts in #eng-sre with: scope, reason, start/end, owner.
- Unplanned suppressions during incident: allowed by oncall, but must be written into the incident notes and followed by a tuning ticket.

F) Oncall enablement
[ ] 30-minute training walkthrough recorded (or live session notes) covering dashboards, alert payload, and first 5 triage steps.
[ ] “What to do first” checklist included at top of runbook.
[ ] Confirm access: SRE + Runtime oncalls have Grafana dashboard access and metrics namespace permissions (INT-3321).

G) Communication + tooling
Channels
- Paging: PagerDuty service “Perf Canary Regressions” (routes to SRE primary).
- Triage coordination: #eng-oncall; Runtime deep dive: #eng-runtime.
- Incident channel: #inc-perf-canary-YYYYMMDD (create when mitigation/rollback required).

Alert payload must include
- Model, region, gpu_sku, scheduler_mode
- Metric name + window + sample size
- Baseline strategy (rolling 7d median vs pinned)
- Latest runtime_build/runtime_version/git_sha + last deploy timestamp
- Links: dashboard, runbook, recent deploy diff view

Acceptance criteria
- Checklist reviewed by SRE lead (Sean) + Runtime perf architect (Noah).
- Linked from ENG-2841 and from the phase-1 rollout ticket (ENG-2850).
- Used in at least one “test page” dry run with responders following the checklist end-to-end.

Open questions
- Do we want a “ticket-first” default for the first 2 weeks of eu-west expansion, or keep paging and rely on broader suppression windows?
- Should we require dual-confirmation (two slices or two consecutive windows) before paging for tokens/sec-only regressions?

Deliverable
- Confluence page: “Perf Canary Operational Readiness Checklist (v1)” and link added to runbook + alert policy pages.
comments: 2026-01-28 (Tomáš Novák): Drafted checklist sections A–D. Need confirmation from Connor on runtime rollback mechanics (do we always have a pinned known-good build per region?).
2026-01-30 (Sean Gallagher): Looks good. Strong preference: paging only after 72h ticket-only and at least one planned suppression dry-run. Add explicit guidance on avoiding blanket suppressions.

2026-02-02 (Noah Patel): Added note: for suspected kernel regression tied to runtime build, rollback is preferred over trying to “pin scheduler mode” as a mitigation. Scheduler pinning is for variance reduction, not mitigation.

2026-02-06 (Rafael Mendes): PD service created and test paging done; please add the PD service name + runbook link into the required payload section. Also add dedup key reminder (model+region+gpu_sku+metric).

2026-02-11 (Logan Wright): Please ensure the payload requirements don’t include high-cardinality fields like kernel_id by default. Kernel debug export should remain gated behind canary-tag and only used in manual debug, not alert labels.
